checks.label: A moment is the turning effect of a force: the arm pushes each mass with the torque ÷ r, and that push acting r out gives back the same torque at every radius
Rotational power needs the speed converted to rad/s: 40 N m at 960 rev/min is 40 × 100.5 = 4.02 kW, where 40 × 960 would give 38.4 kW
A flywheel stores more energy with a higher moment of inertia, from more mass or mass further from its centre: at full speed every step out stores more
The opening rig: I = 2 × 25 × 0.2² = 2 kg m², 50 N m adds 25 rad/s each second, and 1450 rev/min (151.8 rad/s) comes in 6.1 s with 23.1 kJ stored; at 0.1 m I is 0.5 kg m²
Twice the radius, four times the run-up: at every torque, masses 0.4 m out take 4 times as long as at 0.2 m (24.3 s against 6.1 s at 50 N m) and store 4 times the energy (92.2 kJ)
A steady net torque draws a straight speed line, the same rise every second, and the energy at half speed is a quarter of the energy at full speed
The motor sketch gives 130 N m at rest, peaks at 276 N m at 1125 rev/min and falls to 0 at 1500 rev/min; the pump takes 72.4 N m at 1450 rev/min, and they meet near 1450 rev/min
Motor and pump: the speed rises all the way but never passes where the curves meet, and the run-up to 1435 rev/min, 99% of it, takes 1.9 s on 2 kg m²
Every puzzle answer is worked from its rule: 8 kg m², 1.9 s, 4.02 kW, 23.1 kJ, 3.8 s and 0 N m, with the wrong picks 4, 20, 18.1, 7.6, 640 W, 38.4, 11.5, 36.0, 12.6 and 144.8
Each puzzle offers three answers and accepts only its right one; every wrong answer has its own hint and its working drawn in red, and nothing is marked before Check
Every run plays time four times faster than real, every demonstration ends within 7 s of its screen opening, and every answer is drawn within 2.5 s of Check
Every screen that shows an idea says it in 90 words or fewer
